clues: This port city sits at the head of a bay, where two small rivers join to form its river. The river runs through the city center into the bay.
The sea is close, and it keeps this town warm in winter. Towns far from the shore feel the cold much more.
Lawmakers met in this city's Old State House for a long stretch, from 1762 to 1904. The port grew rich, and it held on to the seat of government.
Roger Williams set up this town in 1636, when he was cast out for his faith. He made it a home where all could pray as they wished.
Rhode Island's governor works in this town, the state's biggest. Its lawmakers meet in the white marble State House.
